ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is a straight line, and $OD$, $OE$ are the angle bisectors of $\angle AOC$, $\angle BOC$, respectively. If $\angle BOC = \alpha$, what is $\angle DOE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB$ is a straight line, and $OD, OE$ are the bisectors of $\angle AOC, \angle BOC$ respectively,\\
thus $\angle 1=\angle EOB=\frac{1}{2}\angle BOC$\\
thus $\angle DOC=\angle AOD=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOC$,\\
thus $\angle DOE=\angle 1+\angle 2=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOC+\frac{1}{2}\angle BOC=90^\circ=\boxed{90^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows AB as a horizontal straight line passing through O, with A on the left and B on the right. Above O, the rays appear in the order OD, OC, OE from left to right, so ∠DOE is the sum of the adjacent angles ∠DOC and ∠COE. Reasoning: Given ∠BOC = α. Since AB is a straight line, ∠AOC + ∠BOC = 180°, hence ∠AOC = 180° − α. OD bisects ∠AOC, so ∠DOC = (180° − α)/2. OE bisects ∠BOC, so ∠COE = α/2. Therefore ∠DOE = ∠DOC + ∠COE = (180° − α)/2 + α/2 = 90°.
